pipeline {

    agent any

    stages {

        stage('SCM Checkout') {
            steps {

                git 'https://github.com/victor-tan-hk/DotNetWebApp.git'
            }
        }

        stage('Clean') {
            steps {
                /*
                 * Remove build artifacts left in the current workspace
                 * from a previous run.
                 *
                 * Remove test reports and published application files
                 * generated by previous pipeline runs.
                 *
                 * This prevents Jenkins from accidentally processing
                 * stale test reports from an earlier build.                 
                 *
                 */
                sh '''
                    dotnet clean DotNetWebApp.slnx \
                        --configuration Release

                    rm -rf "${WORKSPACE}/artifacts/test-results"
                    rm -rf "${WORKSPACE}/artifacts/publish"
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Restore') {
            steps {
                /*
                 * Download the NuGet packages required by the application
                 * and test projects.
                 */
                sh '''
                    dotnet restore DotNetWebApp.slnx
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Build') {
            steps {
                /*
                * Build the application and test project in Release mode.
                *
                * --no-restore prevents a second implicit package restore
                * because the Restore stage has already completed it.
                */                 
                sh '''

                    dotnet build DotNetWebApp.slnx \
                        --configuration Release \
                        --no-restore

                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Test') {

            steps {
                /*
                *
                * Execute all unit tests.
                *
                * --no-build
                *     Uses the assemblies generated during the Build stage.
                *
                * --no-restore
                *     Prevents another NuGet package restore.
                *
                * --logger trx
                *     Writes the test results in Microsoft's TRX format.
                *     TRX is a machine-readable XML-based test-report format.
                *
                * --results-directory
                *     Stores the generated TRX files in a predictable
                *     workspace directory so Jenkins can find them later.         
                *        
                */
                sh '''

                    mkdir -p "${WORKSPACE}/artifacts/test-results"

                    dotnet test DotNetWebApp.slnx \
                        --configuration Release \
                        --no-build \
                        --no-restore \
                        --logger "trx" \
                        --results-directory \
                        "${WORKSPACE}/artifacts/test-results"

                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Publish') {
            steps {
                /*
                 * Publish a framework-dependent Linux application.
                 *
                 * --no-build reuses the successful Release build.
                 */
                sh '''
                    dotnet publish "src/DotNetWebApp.Api/DotNetWebApp.Api.csproj" \
                        --configuration Release \
                        --no-build \
                        --output "${WORKSPACE}/artifacts/publish"

                    echo "Published files:"

                    find "${WORKSPACE}/artifacts/publish" \
                        -maxdepth 2 \
                        -type f \
                        -print
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Deploy') {
            steps {
                /*
                 * Run the published web app application once.
                 *
                 * This is a simple deployment verification or smoke test
                 * confirming that the published web app can start.
                 */
                sh '''
                
                    dotnet "${WORKSPACE}/artifacts/publish/DotNetWebApp.Api.dll" \
                    --urls http://0.0.0.0:8080                

                '''
            }
        }
    }

    /*
     * Pipeline-level post actions run after the stages have completed.
     *
     * The "always" condition means that Jenkins attempts to process the test
     * results regardless of whether the pipeline succeeds, fails or becomes
     * unstable.
     *
     * This is particularly important when unit tests fail. The dotnet test
     * command returns a non-zero exit code when a test fails, causing the
     * Test stage to fail. The post action can still process the generated
     * TRX report and show which tests failed.
     */

    post {
        always {

            /*
             * Publish every TRX test-result file generated under the
             * test-results directory.
             *
             * The Jenkins MSTest plugin converts the TRX results into the
             * internal test-result representation used by Jenkins.

            * Do not fail the pipeline merely because the publisher
            * encounters a report-processing problem.
            *
            * Actual test failures are still reported by dotnet test.

            * Preserve test standard output in the Jenkins test report.
            * This can help diagnose failed tests, although it can consume
            * more Jenkins storage when tests produce extensive output.
            */


            mstest(
                testResultsFile:
                    'artifacts/test-results/**/*.trx',
                failOnError: false,
                keepLongStdio: true
            )


            /*
             * Archive all files generated within the artifacts directory.
             *
             * This normally includes:
             *
             *   artifacts/test-results/
             *       TRX unit-test reports
             *
             *   artifacts/publish/
             *       Published application assemblies, configuration files
             *       and other runtime dependencies
             *

             * Do not fail the post section when no artifact files exist.
             *
             * For example, an early Restore or Build failure could occur
             * before either the Test or Publish stage creates files.

             * Generate fingerprints for archived files. 
             * Fingerprints help Jenkins track where identical artifacts
             * were produced or subsequently used by other jobs.

             * The archived files are retained as artifacts belonging to
             * this specific Jenkins build and can be downloaded through
             * the Jenkins build UI.
             */
            archiveArtifacts(
                artifacts: 'artifacts/**/*',
                allowEmptyArchive: true,
                fingerprint: true
            )

        }
    }
}
